free_local_only_constraint_investigation.method: read-only code inspection of studio_router.rank()/select() and evolution/advance.py._rank_engineering_engines()/_implementation_router()
free_local_only_constraint_investigation.finding: No existing parameter, flag, or canonical mechanism lets a caller constrain routing to free/local-only. studio_router.rank() surfaces cost_class per candidate but does not filter by it. The actual engine choice among accepted candidates is made by _rank_engineering_engines()'s internal duty-cycle weighting, which is not caller-configurable and currently favors claude_code.
options_considered_and_rejected: Adding a free-only filter/parameter to the router -- rejected: would be engineering a new constraint into the canonical router, which this campaign was explicitly told not to do

Manually marking claude_code_engineer_v1 as quota-limited in the registry to force omni_engineer selection -- rejected: this would be gaming/tampering with live capability data to manufacture a predetermined outcome, not a genuine existing constraint, and would itself be a form of hidden manipulation

Running a second canary anyway and hoping duty-cycle favors omni_engineer this time -- rejected: not deterministic, and the audit evidence shows the current duty weighting (0.1 vs 0.4) actively favors claude_code, so a second attempt would most likely repeat the same paid selection rather than prove a free-only path
free_local_only_constraint_investigation.conclusion: No genuine canonical free/local-only constraint exists today. No second canary was run.
